content: <thought>From the spectrum we see a clear M+1 peak (~13 % of the monoisotopic intensity) indicating the presence of carbon (13 C natural abundance ≈1 % per carbon atom). The M+2 peak is relatively strong (~33 % of the monoisotopic intensity), which matches the characteristic isotopic pattern of chlorine (35Cl/37Cl ≈ 3:1). No other element shows a distinctive isotopic signature (e.g., bromine would give an M+2 ≈ 100 % of M, sulfur would give only a few percent). Therefore the elements that can be definitively identified are carbon and chlorine.
